chapters.intro: How to ask for the way and understand the answer when someone points you somewhere. Tap 🔊 to hear each Dutch phrase spoken.

sections.title: Stay polite
sections.body: Start with Pardon or Sorry to get attention, then ask your question. Use the polite u (not je) with strangers on the street. End with Dank u wel.

sections.title: Richtingen
sections.note: The core direction words. Learn these first.

items.en: the first street on the left
the second street on the right

items.nl: tot het einde van de straat
items.en: to the end of the street

sections.title: Waar is het? (plaats)
sections.note: Words that say where something is in relation to other things.

sections.title: Handige plekken
sections.note: Common landmarks people use to point the way.

sections.title: De weg vragen (zinnen)
sections.note: Full sentences you can use right away.

items.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

items.nl: Hoe kom ik bij de supermarkt?
items.en: How do I get to the supermarket?
How long does it take to walk?

items.nl: Kunt u het op de kaart laten zien?
items.en: Can you show it on the map?

sections.title: Understanding the answer
sections.body: Listen for ga (go), loop (walk) and sla af (turn). For example: Ga rechtdoor en sla de eerste straat links af means Go straight ahead and take the first street on the left.

sections.q: U bent verdwaald. Wat vraagt u aan iemand op straat?
sections.qEn: You are lost. What do you ask someone on the street?
options: Pardon, hoe kom ik bij het station?
Ik woon hier al tien jaar.
sections.answer: Pardon, hoe kom ik bij het station?
sections.explanation: Pardon politely gets attention and Hoe kom ik bij...? is the standard way to ask how to get somewhere. The other options do not ask for directions.

chapters.intro: What to say on the phone and how to make or change an appointment with a doctor, the town hall or a company. Tap 🔊 to hear each phrase.

sections.title: Answering the phone
sections.body: In Dutch you usually answer with your own name: Met Anna. (literally With Anna). The caller replies U spreekt met... or Met... and then their name. Speak a little slower than usual.

items.en: Good morning, this is the doctor practice.
Can I speak to the doctor?

sections.title: Een boodschap
sections.note: When the person is not available.

items.en: He is not here right now.
Can you pass on a message?

items.nl: Dat is goed, dank u wel.

items.en: Have a good rest of the day.

items.nl: Ik wil graag een afspraak maken.
items.en: I would like to make an appointment.
Does Tuesday at ten o clock work?

items.nl: Heeft u iets in de ochtend?
items.en: Do you have anything in the morning?

items.nl: Heeft u iets in de middag?
items.en: Do you have anything in the afternoon?

items.nl: Hoe laat moet ik er zijn?
items.en: What time should I be there?
How long does the appointment take?
Where do I need to be?
I have to reschedule the appointment.
I have to cancel the appointment.
Can it be a day later?
Can it be an hour earlier?

items.nl: Sorry dat ik zo laat bel.

sections.title: Numbers on the phone
sections.body: Dutch phone numbers are read in pairs: 06 12 34 56 78 is nul zes, twaalf, vierendertig, zesenvijftig, achtenzeventig. If you miss it, say Kunt u het langzaam herhalen?

sections.q: De receptie zegt: De dokter is er niet. Wat zegt u?
sections.qEn: The receptionist says: The doctor is not here. What do you say?
sections.explanation: When the person you want is unavailable, you ask the receptionist to pass on a message with Kunt u een boodschap doorgeven? The other options do not fit a phone call.

chapters.intro: The words you need in an emergency, plus the names of the Dutch institutions you will deal with as a newcomer. Tap 🔊 to hear each phrase.

sections.title: Call 112 in an emergency
sections.body: Bel 112 for the police, fire brigade or ambulance when there is real danger or someone is badly hurt. For medical help that is not urgent, call the huisartsenpost (the after-hours GP service). 112 is free and works without credit.

sections.title: Hulp vragen
sections.note: Short, clear phrases for an emergency. Say them loudly.

sections.title: Wat is er gebeurd?
sections.note: The 112 operator will ask questions like these.

items.nl: Wat is er aan de hand?

sections.title: Belangrijke instanties
sections.note: The Dutch bodies you will deal with as a newcomer. Learn what each one does.

items.en: the municipality (town hall) — registration, ID and local matters
your digital ID to log in to government websites
your citizen service number, used for everything official
the tax office — taxes and benefits (toeslagen)
the agency for work and unemployment benefits
your GP — your first contact for medical care
the pharmacy — where you collect your medicine

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: You always need a verwijzing (referral) from your huisarts to see a specialist. Your zorgverzekering (health insurance) is compulsory in the Netherlands. Keep your BSN and DigiD details safe and never share them by email.

sections.q: Er is een groot ongeluk en iemand is zwaargewond. Wat doet u?
sections.qEn: There is a serious accident and someone is badly injured. What do you do?
sections.explanation: In a real emergency with a badly injured person you call 112 for the ambulance and police. The pharmacy and the town hall do not handle emergencies.
